title: TerminalVibes artwork review
artDirection: Rich, carefully composed educational illustration for an adult beginner. Keep the affectionate hermit crab and garden world, with believable anatomy, tactile materials, and delightful incidental detail. Vary the palette and the visual setting across the course; use corals, cobalt, lilac, warm ivory, terracotta, citrus, jade, and night-sky blue with controlled contrast. Complexity should reward looking without obscuring the one teaching action. Leave room for accurate captions and diagrams to be added as live interface text. No imitation of an existing artist.
guardrails: No baked-in command examples, keyboard labels, dates, numeric output, dense prose, watermarks, or invented interface controls; precise teaching labels belong in HTML/SVG overlays.
Rich illustration is supporting evidence, never the only explanation. Match the visual checks for the concept.
Keep anatomy, light sources, reflections, object counts, folder identities, and transformation direction internally consistent.
Produce an actual distinct image for each alternative, not five crops or recolors of one composition. Do not select or replace any course illustration without the user choosing it.

variantDirections.name: Daylight storybook
variantDirections.brief: Detailed painterly editorial illustration in a sunlit garden, warm ivory and terracotta balanced by cobalt and fresh foliage. Use an intimate eye-level composition with one strong central teaching action and a few rich supporting details.

variantDirections.name: Colorful miniature
variantDirections.brief: Tactile miniature diorama, broad three-quarter perspective, ceramic tools and paper notes, coral and turquoise accented with golden yellow. Give objects real depth and make the before/after relationship readable spatially.

variantDirections.name: Open workshop
variantDirections.brief: An intricate cutaway or overhead workshop arrangement, indigo, peach, mint, and natural wood. Use clear spatial connections and repeated object identity to explain the process, with generous pale breathing room around the main action.

variantDirections.name: Layered field guide
variantDirections.brief: Sophisticated layered paper-and-ink field-guide illustration with tangible paper edges, violet, russet, sea glass, and warm white. Create a connected sequence of generous vignettes; preserve expressive character and botanical detail without tiny text.

variantDirections.name: Lantern evening
variantDirections.brief: Luminous blue-hour garden scene, deep cobalt and plum balanced by amber lanterns, coral flowers, and cyan reflections. Use a cinematic close foreground and softly lit depth; keep the essential action brighter and clearer than the decorative surroundings.

reviewNotes: No alternative is selected initially. Choices are local to the review browser until exported.
Existing alt text is preserved as inventory evidence; proposed alt text must be revised against the actual selected image.
The two earlier v2 illustration drafts remain unapproved. Import them deliberately into a chosen candidate slot only if they fit its concept and format.

The current og-image.png is a branded social preview; its replacement is derived from the approved hero. Favicons are derived from the approved logo. UI screenshots and generated timeline crops are derived assets, not independent illustration concepts.

concepts.title: Your first small success
concepts.purpose: Connect typing one instruction to seeing a reply immediately.
concepts.visualBrief: A curious hermit crab at an inviting garden workbench presses one key; a single luminous reply appears on a modest terminal. Early morning flowers, terracotta pots, cobalt tools and coral details create a world worth exploring. Leave the screen simple enough for a live hello-world overlay.
visualChecks: The crab is doing one small action, not admiring a huge mysterious machine. Keep the terminal and visible reply the clear focus.
concepts.altSuggestion: A curious hermit crab at an inviting garden workbench presses one key; a single luminous reply appears on a modest terminal.

concepts.visualBrief: A glass garden apiary contains several active workshop cells, with two running instances fed from the same stored blueprint. Each cell has a different blank number plaque and its own activity.
visualChecks: A process is an instance, not the executable file itself. Leave PID numbers to an accessible overlay rather than tiny invented text.
concepts.altSuggestion: A glass garden apiary contains several active workshop cells, with two running instances fed from the same stored blueprint.

sourceRefs.alt: A glass apiary with a separate numbered cell for each running program.
sourceRefs.caption: A process is a running program. Its PID identifies that instance.

concepts.title: Ask a process to stop
concepts.purpose: Distinguish interrupting the foreground job from sending termination signals to a chosen process.
concepts.visualBrief: A crab sends a gentle stop request to one busy workshop cell and waits for it to tidy up. A separate sealed emergency stop tool remains unused. A final empty cell shows verification that the job ended.
visualChecks: A stop request may be handled or ignored. Do not depict TERM and KILL as equivalent or suggest KILL permits cleanup.
concepts.altSuggestion: A crab sends a gentle stop request to one busy workshop cell and waits for it to tidy up.

sourceRefs.alt: A green TERM message beside a sealed red KILL message.
sourceRefs.caption: Interrupt the foreground job; request termination of another process; verify the result.

concepts.title: Find who is using the port
concepts.purpose: Connect a local listening port to the particular process owning it.
concepts.visualBrief: A small harbor gate is occupied by one identifiable service boat, while another waits outside. A harbor register links the gate to that boat; the crab reads it before deciding what to stop.
visualChecks: The number denotes a listening endpoint, not the PID. No automatic eviction or dangerous kill-all message.
concepts.altSuggestion: A small harbor gate is occupied by one identifiable service boat, while another waits outside.

concepts.purpose: Show foreground interaction and background work sharing a terminal.

concepts.title: This machine, this port
concepts.purpose: Make localhost relative to the computer where the request runs.

visualChecks: Both machines have their own localhost. Do not imply a shared global machine or that every numbered port has a running service.

sourceRefs.alt: A lighthouse directs its beam inward toward numbered doors on its own island.

concepts.title: Follow the shape of JSON
concepts.purpose: Connect named object members, nested objects, and array positions.

visualChecks: Objects and arrays must be visually distinct. Do not generate a wall of malformed JSON; exact sample data belongs in live code.

concepts.title: Keep credentials out of transcripts
concepts.purpose: Explain that a credential can leak through command history and shared output.
concepts.visualBrief: A credential card is stored inside a secure envelope while a public command-history scroll remains free of its contents. A crab chooses a safe empty placeholder card when showing the work to a friend.

sourceRefs.alt: A safe holds a credential card beside a command-history scroll.

concepts.title: The hermit crab guide
concepts.purpose: Give the course a welcoming recognizable identity that survives small display sizes.

visualChecks: Anatomy must be coherent: paired claws, believable legs, consistent shell opening. The outline must remain readable at 24 pixels; no miniature terminal text.
